title: Choose Hootnote's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Railway Timetable. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Railway Timetable
options.lineage: Swiss and European printed railway timetables (Kursbuch, station departure posters)
options.thesis: Your day of calls set like a timetable: every meeting and every sentence keeps its time in one aligned column.
materials: signal red for now and live
options.viewport: Native sidebar (Home, Meetings, Dictations). Home leads with three actions: record in person, upload audio, dictation. Below, Today set as a timetable: time, line (app or speaker), title, duration, state. A red now-line marks the current time.
options.risk: Reads cold and utilitarian if alignment slips; the column rhythm has to be exact everywhere.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: large tabular times carry the timetable, no boxes or cards.
One strict armature: the time column has the same width on Home, in the meeting list and in every transcript.
A fixed state sequence: Recording, Transcribing, Ready always sit in the same place with the same words.
Nothing jumps: a meeting's state changes where it sits; rows never reorder while you read.
The next meeting is one keystroke away: up and down arrows move through the day.

options.label: Certified Transcript
options.thesis: The verbatim record: who said what, attested line by line.
options.viewport: Native sidebar; Home leads with the three actions, then recent meetings as entries in a record index, each with its line count and speakers.
options.risk: The most familiar choice: it is closest to what transcript apps already look like, and can read legalistic.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.lineage: software built in one neutral scale with a single accent
options.thesis: Almost no color: one neutral scale, one accent used only for what is live.
options.viewport: Native sidebar; Home as a quiet grid: actions row, recent meetings list, dictations list, all in grays with the accent only on Record.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds product clarity; loses on identification because it is the category's own default look.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from many tools; the mode rules call a gray screen with one accent the category default.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.case: Consultants travel, but meetings as tear-off coupons costume a working screen.
options.kept: States change in place and never vanish.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.case: No link to meetings or transcripts; a specimen is a showcase, not a work tool.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.case: Poster logic; a visible construction grid would crowd transcripts.
options.kept: One strict grid as the armature.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.case: Cream-and-engraving softness contradicts the strictly professional brief.
options.kept: A fixed, named sequence of states.

options.label: Vertical Media Feed
options.case: One item per screen fights scanning a day of meetings.
options.kept: The next item is always one step away.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What meeting-notes apps ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of meetings, a large Record button, recent meetings as a list with blue accents.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
